Source: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/575643/re-elected-christchurch-mayor-to-focus-on-debt-liveability
Title: Re-elected Christchurch mayor to focus on debt, liveability
Chunks: 0,1
Christchurch mayor Phil Mauger is grateful to be re-elected for a second term and wants to keep the city's momentum going.
Progress results on Saturday 11 October show Mauger has won the mayoralty with 54,644 votes, a majority of almost 20,000.
His nearest rival, third-term councillor Sara Templeton, received 34,726 votes.
As progress results stand, Mauger will be joined at the council table by two new councillors and 14 returning councillors.
Mauger was celebrating the result on Saturday.
"I was always pretty confident that I'd get there, but I've actually been blown away by how grateful I am for the people of Christchurch to give me a mandate of that size," he said.
Mauger thought voters were won over by the "pragmatic" way he approached issues.
"How I want to get things done, trying to cut red tape and just make Christchurch a better place to live," he said.
"I've just got to try harder and make sure that we continue the momentum that Christchurch has got going forward for the next three years.
"I want Christchurch to be - and it's certainly getting there - the sporting and events capital of the country."
Mauger said one of the biggest challenges facing the new council was debt.
"We've got to look at debt. Debt is all right in some people's eyes a little bit and I'm happy to have some debt, but I feel we've got too much. So if we pay down some debt and have got a little bit more up our sleeve to use ratepayer money towards doing the things that people want."
Mauger was elected mayor in 2022 but had served on the Christchurch City Council since 2019.
His campaign was focused on delivering practical results and planning for Christchurch's long-term and prosperous growth.
Sara Templeton, who resigned her council seat to run for mayor, thanked her campaign team and supporters in a Facebook post.
"While today's result wasn't what we hoped for, I'm deeply proud of the positive, future-focused campaign we ran and so grateful to everyone who believed in a better future for our city," Templeton said.

"The twelve years I've spent serving the communities of the Heathcote Ward and our wider city have been incredibly rewarding and motivating. From the rebuild of our community facilities to the creation of the stunning Coastal Pathway, it's been a privilege to play a part in the growth and renewal of Ōtautahi.
"Going into this campaign, I always knew it would be a tough ask to beat an incumbent mayor, but it was important that residents had a real choice. We ran a campaign focused on the issues that matter: fixing infrastructure, building strong communities, and creating a fairer, greener, more connected and resilient city ready to face the challenges ahead."
The next highest polling mayoral candidate was Thomas Healey, who received 1547 votes.

Source: https://www.thepress.co.nz/nz-news/360851360/which-councillors-have-won-christchurch-and-who-has-lost-their-seat
Title: Which councillors have won in Christchurch and who has lost their seat?
Chunks: 0,1
Sinead Gill
Incumbents Jake McLellan, Pauline Cotter, and newcomer Nathaniel Herz Jardine have tenatively won their wards.Composite image / Stuff
It could be back to the future for incumbent mayor Phil Mauger, as an early result for Christchurch in the 2025 local elections sees him leading a council with a near-identical set of colleagues.
All hotly contested wards in Christchurch have been provisionally won by sitting councillors as of Saturday, and the two wards with fresh faces will be represented with a centre-left or centre-right leaning representative, as they have had for the last three years.
But with election day and special votes yet to be counted – and one contest with a margin of 139 votes – it is possible all provisional winners will be waiting to celebrate.
The progress results represented about 85% of all votes to be counted in this election, meaning some 14,000 ballots across the 16 wards are still to come.
Candidates Raf Manji, Tony Simons and Ali Jones have so far been unsuccessful.Stuff
The provisional win for incumbent Pauline Cotter in her rematch against Ali Jones in the Innes ward saw her with 2873 votes, just 139 more than Jones.
Cotter beat Jones by just 16 votes in 2022 after a judicial recount.
Cotter’s running mate in The People’s Choice, Central ward incumbent Jake McLellan, has also managed to hold firm onto his seat, despite running in the most competitive ward in the city, where concerns of vote splitting for candidates like Hayley Guglietta and Tom Roud had some expecting Raf Manji would get a decisive lead.
With a 640-vote lead on the runner-up, McLellan has secured 42% of the vote so far in Central, compared to Manji’s 25%.
In the ward with the worst voter turnout in Christchurch, Riccarton’s Tyla Harrison-Hunt, also of The People’s Choice, will likely be breathing a sigh of relief with 40% of the vote so far, or 406 votes ahead of runner-up, Tony Simons.
Simons, a fierce competitor with a lot of influence in residents association circles, has got 29%.

As for the fresh faces, newcomer David Cartwright, a member of the centre-right Independent Citizens ticket – replacing outgoing James Gough, of the same political leaning – has a decisive margin of 3275 on his runner-up, independent Xavier Dickason.
Heathcote will welcome Nathaniel Herz Jardine as its new representative, replacing Sara Templeton who only ran for the mayoralty. Herz Jardine, with The People’s Choice, has a margin of 1266 on Ian Kearney.
The most decisive winner by far was incumbent Andrei Moore in Halswell, with a whopping 86% of the vote and a margin of 5629 votes.
The remaining ward contests have also seen their sitting councillors re-elected.

The progress results represented about 85% of all votes to be counted in this election, meaning some 14,000 ballots across the 16 wards are still to come.
Candidates Raf Manji, Tony Simons and Ali Jones have so far been unsuccessful.Stuff

16 May 2022
Local authority elections will be held on Saturday, 8 October this year. This notice tells you how to enrol, and who can enrol as a ratepayer elector, so you can vote in the elections.
The Electoral Roll closes on Friday, 12 August 2022. If you enrol after this date, you will need to cast a ‘special vote’ at the election.
You can vote by post. Make sure you are on the Electoral Roll to receive your postal voting document.

## You can only enrol once
You can only enrol, or be nominated to enrol, once in a council district, no matter how many properties you own in that council district.

## What Council District means in this notice
Council district includes:
*   city, district and regional council areas  
*   a community board area, if established  
*   the area of Auckland Council and the local boards.

## Residential Electors
If you are registered to vote in Parliamentary elections (a Parliamentary elector), you are automatically enrolled as a residential elector to vote in local authority elections. The address where you are registered as a Parliamentary elector must be in the council district for the local authority elections.

## Ratepayer Electors
You may be eligible to enrol as a non-resident ratepayer elector in a council district if both of these apply:
*   you are on the district valuation roll and pay rates in the council district  
*   the address where you are registered as a Parliamentary elector is outside that council district.
Your eligibility to enrol or be nominated as a ratepayer may also depend on your individual circumstances as determined by criteria in the Local Electoral Act 2001 and its regulations.

## Ratepayer Electors
### If more than one person pays rates on the same property
If partners, joint tenants and tenants in common collectively pay rates on a property in a council district, one of the group may be nominated to go on the Electoral Roll. The person nominating and the nominated person must be registered as Parliamentary electors at addresses outside the council district where the property is located.

## Ratepayer Electors
### Existing Ratepayer Electors should have received an enrolment confirmation form
New Electoral Rolls are compiled every three years for the local authority elections.
You should already have an enrolment confirmation form or other advice on your ratepayer elector status if:
*   you were enrolled as a ratepayer elector for the 2019 local authority elections, or since then

*   you enrolled or were nominated as a ratepayer elector.
Do not have your enrolment confirmation form?
Contact the local council you pay rates to, or call (freephone) 0800 54 8683 if:
*   you are still waiting to receive your Enrolment Confirmation Form or other advice about your non-resident ratepayer status  
*   you have misplaced your Enrolment Confirmation Form.

## Ratepayer Electors
### New Ratepayer Electors who wish to enrol or nominate a Ratepayer Elector
If you think you may be eligible to enrol or to nominate someone as a ratepayer elector:
*   get an Enrolment Form for Ratepayer Electors from the local council where you pay your rates  
*   get this form early so you can get answers to any questions you have about the form or being on the Electoral Roll before the roll closes on Friday, 12 August 2022.
Jo Daly, Christchurch City Council Electoral Officer will be able to help you with your application.
This public notice is issued pursuant to Section 39(1)(a), Local Electoral Act 2001.
Jo Daly
Electoral Officer

16 May 2022
Local authority elections will be held on Saturday, 8 October this year. This notice tells you how to enrol, and who can enrol as a ratepayer elector, so you can vote in the elections.
The Electoral Roll closes on Friday, 12 August 2022. If you enrol after this date, you will need to cast a ‘special vote’ at the election.
You can vote by post. Make sure you are on the Electoral Roll to receive your postal voting document.

## You can only enrol once
You can only enrol, or be nominated to enrol, once in a council district, no matter how many properties you own in that council district.

## What Council District means in this notice
Council district includes:
*   city, district and regional council areas  
*   a community board area, if established  
*   the area of Auckland Council and the local boards.

## Residential Electors
If you are registered to vote in Parliamentary elections (a Parliamentary elector), you are automatically enrolled as a residential elector to vote in local authority elections. The address where you are registered as a Parliamentary elector must be in the council district for the local authority elections.

## Ratepayer Electors
You may be eligible to enrol as a non-resident ratepayer elector in a council district if both of these apply:
*   you are on the district valuation roll and pay rates in the council district  
*   the address where you are registered as a Parliamentary elector is outside that council district.
Your eligibility to enrol or be nominated as a ratepayer may also depend on your individual circumstances as determined by criteria in the Local Electoral Act 2001 and its regulations.

## Ratepayer Electors
### If more than one person pays rates on the same property
If partners, joint tenants and tenants in common collectively pay rates on a property in a council district, one of the group may be nominated to go on the Electoral Roll. The person nominating and the nominated person must be registered as Parliamentary electors at addresses outside the council district where the property is located.

## Ratepayer Electors
### Existing Ratepayer Electors should have received an enrolment confirmation form
New Electoral Rolls are compiled every three years for the local authority elections.
You should already have an enrolment confirmation form or other advice on your ratepayer elector status if:
*   you were enrolled as a ratepayer elector for the 2019 local authority elections, or since then

*   you enrolled or were nominated as a ratepayer elector.
Do not have your enrolment confirmation form?
Contact the local council you pay rates to, or call (freephone) 0800 54 8683 if:
*   you are still waiting to receive your Enrolment Confirmation Form or other advice about your non-resident ratepayer status  
*   you have misplaced your Enrolment Confirmation Form.

## Ratepayer Electors
### New Ratepayer Electors who wish to enrol or nominate a Ratepayer Elector
If you think you may be eligible to enrol or to nominate someone as a ratepayer elector:
*   get an Enrolment Form for Ratepayer Electors from the local council where you pay your rates  
*   get this form early so you can get answers to any questions you have about the form or being on the Electoral Roll before the roll closes on Friday, 12 August 2022.
